parsed.explanation: The counterexample is valid: for F={{1,2},{2,3}} and transversal C={2}, X={1,3} traverses F but does not meet C, so the displayed criterion omits it. In recursive applications, C\{c} need not belong to F_c, so the induction hypothesis has only been argued for a restricted class of transversals. Moreover, the stated general finite-transversal lemma is false for arbitrary pairwise-intersecting families, as noted in L6.2. The later finite list and periodicity argument depend on it, while the approaches/status sections merely assert finiteness. A valid number-theoretic large-prime-erasure lemma must replace this step.
